issue.title: Add Cloudflare to Flask Hosting Platforms docs?

summary.text: This is a documentation request to add Cloudflare Workers to Flask’s Hosting Platforms page. After discussing concerns about commercial links, a maintainer invited the reporter to open a pull request and separately share the Pallets donation link.

known_facts.text: The reporter says Cloudflare Workers supports Flask applications and links to a deployment guide.
A maintainer initially noted that the Cloudflare examples repository did not contain the referenced example; the reporter subsequently said it had been merged.
A maintainer expressed concern that company-submitted hosting links can feel like advertising, while noting that Cloudflare is comparable in scale to platforms already listed.
The maintainer clarified that a donation would not promise any particular service, provided the Pallets donation page, and later invited the reporter to open a pull request and pass along that link.
The recorded searches found no eligible related issue candidates for the Cloudflare hosting or Hosting Platforms documentation queries.

missing_information: Whether the reporter intends to open the invited documentation pull request and pass the donation link to the appropriate Cloudflare team.

label_recommendations.name: docs
label_recommendations.reason: The requested change is specifically an addition to Flask’s Hosting Platforms documentation.

draft_reply: Thanks for adding the missing example to Cloudflare’s repository. A PR adding the Cloudflare guide to the Hosting Platforms documentation would be welcome for review. Separately, please pass along https://palletsprojects.com/donate internally if appropriate; as noted above, any donation would not promise placement or another particular service. Are you able to open the documentation PR?
limitations: The current Flask documentation, Cloudflare guide, examples repository, source code, and release history were not independently inspected.
The two repository issue searches returned no eligible candidates, but that does not rule out a differently worded related or duplicate issue.
